location_qualifier: OB West HQ; location per Rundstedt biography
current_activity: holding reserve panzer divisions at OKW disposal; HQ near Paris
notes: Rundstedt's HQ at Saint-Germain-en-Laye near Paris. Four panzer-type divisions (1st SS, 12th SS, 17th SS PzG, Panzer Lehr) were OKW reserve, released in stages after D-Day. Army Group G (south/west France) also under OB West.

current_activity: meeting Hitler at Margival; ordered to hold positions
notes: Hitler met Rundstedt and Rommel at Wolfsschlucht II (Margival) 16-17 June; Rommel urged ending the war; Hitler ordered fighting positions held (no withdrawal).

current_activity: Rundstedt relieved; Kluge arrives to take over as commander in chief in the west
notes: Event date: Hitler relieved Rundstedt on 2 July 1944 (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 2 p. 28); Kluge was arriving to replace him at the beginning of July (ch. 3 p. 47); the Wikipedia list of OB West commanders gives Kluge from 2 July. Event support: the event itself is stated in the cited text (see Event date); only the headquarters place is a representative point. Location support fallback: no source read gives the headquarters place for 2 July; the point is Saint-Germain-en-Laye, where claim C0013 places Rundstedt's headquarters on 6 June, used as a representative point.

location_qualifier: OB West command post not stated in the source
current_activity: Kluge takes over the command of OB West at 2000 hours on 3 July, the day after Rundstedt was replaced
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary (KTB 1944, western theater, p. 324): "Am 2. 7. wurde der OB West, Gen.-Feldm. v. Rundstedt, durch den Gen.-Feldm. v. Kluge ersetzt (Übernahme des Befehls 3. 7., 20.00 Uhr)"; the replacement is dated 2 July and the takeover of command 3 July, 2000 hours. Event definition: this row is the takeover of command on 3 July at 2000 hours; the 2 July row C0713 is the relief of Rundstedt and Kluge's arrival, so the two rows are different events and not alternatives. Location: the war diary gives no place for the OB West command post; the point is Saint-Germain-en-Laye, the OB West seat used by C0713, with a precision of 25 km. Location support fallback: fallback point only; the source gives no place. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Günther von Kluge, named by the war diary. Event support: good: the war diary of the OKW names the replacement, the day and the hour of the takeover; one source family.

current_activity: Rundstedt is again appointed OB West; the OB West headquarters moves to Koblenz
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary (KTB 1944, western theater, p. 364): "1. 9. der frühere OB West, Gen.-Feldm. v. Rundstedt" is named as the man put back as OB West, with Westphal as chief of staff; the same day's entry says "Der OB verlegte sein Hauptquartier nach Koblenz". Event definition: the appointment of Rundstedt (arrival at the Führer headquarters, 1 September); the takeover of command in the main OB West headquarters near Koblenz is 5 September, in the next row, so the two rows are different events and not alternatives. Event support: Rundstedt's reappointment is dated by the war diary; the move of the headquarters is stated in the entry of the same day (1 September) without a time. Location: Koblenz, the place the war diary names for the OB West headquarters, with a precision of 10 km. Location support: the war diary names the town and not a building. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Gerd von Rundstedt. Context: Model had held OB West and Army Group B together since 17 August; the entry says he was overloaded and the Führer separated the two posts again. Review (German Batch 2 follow-up, 27 October 2026; note only, no value changed): the end of Model's OB West term is described in the note of C0823 (5 September).

current_activity: Rundstedt assumes command in the main OB West headquarters near Koblenz
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 1 p. 42: "On the afternoon of 5 September Rundstedt assumed command in the main OB WEST headquarters near Koblenz"; CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 1 p. 17-18 repeats "After assuming command in the main OB WEST command post near Koblenz". Event definition: the takeover of command at the headquarters on 5 September; Schramm's 1 September row (reappointment) is a different event. Event support: two CMH volumes by different authors state the day; both are one source family. Location: the point is Koblenz with a precision of 25 km, because the source says "near Koblenz" and gives no village. Location approximate: a town point for "near Koblenz". Location support: both CMH passages name the headquarters only as near Koblenz. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Gerd von Rundstedt. Review (German Batch 2 follow-up, 27 October 2026; note and references only, no value changed): the end of Model's OB West term. CMH Breakout and Pursuit ch. 32 p. 700: "While Model remained the Army Group B commander, Rundstedt assumed his old post, Commander-in-Chief, West" (5 September). English Wikipedia, Walter Model: "Model retained command of OB West for eighteen days", counted from 17 August, which ends on 4 September; German Wikipedia (Walter Model, succession box): "16. August – 3. September 1944" for Model as OB West, one to two days earlier than the CMH. So Model held OB West from his arrival on 17 August (or the takeover on 18/19 August, group G018) until 4 or 5 September; Rundstedt's reappointment on 1 September (C0822) preceded his takeover on the afternoon of 5 September (this row); the German Wikipedia 3 September is a noted disagreement and is not recorded as a row. Model stayed the Army Group B commander throughout (CMH p. 700).

current_activity: Rundstedt receives Balck at the OB West headquarters at Bad Kreuznach
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 5 p. 242: "General Balck made a personal visit to Rundstedt's headquarters at Bad Kreuznach"; p. 250 dates the meeting: "Late in the afternoon of the 29th, after a meeting with Field Marshal Rundstedt, General Balck sent word to the First Army". Event definition: the headquarters seen at Bad Kreuznach on 29 September; the move from Koblenz is not dated by any source read. Location: Bad Kreuznach, named by CMH as the place of Rundstedt's headquarters, with a precision of 5 km. Location support: the town is named by the source; the exact building is not. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Gerd von Rundstedt. Context: Balck asked for at least three more divisions and tanks to wipe out the Pont-à-Mousson bridgehead; the same row records the OB West headquarters, not the army group.
